title: Genetic Drift
description: In a small population, chance alone decides which alleles reach the next generation, and every generation a little variation is lost for good. Inbreeding follows, and with it the hidden recessive faults every genome carries. A few migrants a generation are enough to undo it. A species brought back from a handful of genomes has to be bred against this arithmetic, or it dies out a second time. Unlocks the Gene Pool Bench.

puzzle.goal: Each generation a population of N keeps a fraction 1 − 1/(2N) of its heterozygosity. Write H after t generations, from H₀.
puzzle.name: Loss of heterozygosity
puzzle.ask: Find H after t = @{t} generations for N = 50 and H₀ = 0.8.
puzzle.method: Two copies drawn from the same parent gene in a population of N come together with chance 1/(2N); multiply once for each generation.
